counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span explicitly states 'lipoma' as the lead point despite fat density
No histopathologic confirmation of the mass
No raw span for obstructive features or complications
decisive_items: invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen demonstrated a well-defined hypodense lesion measuring 4.6 × 3.4 cm with fat density in the sigmoid-colon wall protruding into the lumen, along with invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
Colonoscopy revealed a 5 × 5 cm exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction occupying half of the lumen
response.rationale: R6 is the only candidate directly anchored to the CT raw span that names intussusception and the fat-density lead mass. R8 only describes the mass without the invagination mechanism. R2 is weakened by normal CEA and fat density rather than malignant features. R7 and R1 rely on nonspecific symptoms/endoscopic exudates and lack the CT-specific intussusception finding.

rejected.why: Normal CEA and fat-density lesion are not raw evidence for sigmoid cancer; the exophytic mass is better explained as a lead point for intussusception.
Colicky pain and mucopurulent discharge are nonspecific; no raw CT or colonoscopy evidence of diverticulitis is supplied.
Mucopurulent discharge and exudates/erosions are nonspecific and contradicted by the CT finding of fat density and intussusception.
